key_insight: A polymorphic AB2O6 high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger greatly boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a route to improve practical photocatalytic carbon conversion by combining materials design for charge handling and surface CO2 adsorption with a renewable biological co-reactant.
method: Designed a bi-polymorph AB2O6 high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, combining layered perovskite and pyrochlore motifs.
Used Cs/Ba to increase surface basicity, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta octahedra for charge transport.
Compared CO2 photoconversion performance with no sacrificial agent, with microplastics, and with microalgae.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using microalgae increases CO and CH4 production by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach depends on maintaining microalgae viability and process integration, so scalability, light management, and biomass handling may limit real-world deployment.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
